rows.notes: Addionics' Tel Aviv pilot line makes 3D-structured aluminium/copper electrodes and current collectors (DigiTimes 2023-02-14), not finished cells; chemistry-agnostic component supplier. v1 already had is_cell_manufacturer=false. Quoted capacity targets (10 kWh to 1 GWh in 2025) are electrode output. BusinessWire release returned 403 so DigiTimes used.

Warners Bay pilot line produces supercapacitors (electrolyte for redox-flow batteries is a future product); no battery cell production. No GWh capacity stated. Allegro's planned gigafactory is a separate, undated, unlocated project.

Renaissance One (Tomago) assembles battery systems/packs from imported cells (S24, 2022: 'continues to import battery cells'); 300 MWh to 5.3 GWh are system/pack figures. Planned in-house cell plant ('Renaissance Two') was never confirmed. The industrial battery business entered administration on 2025-08-13 (S25). If lead prefers to keep a stub, alternative would be update with status null; rejected because no cell production evidence exists.
RenewEconomy 2024-12-04: PowerCap makes and assembles modules in Queensland but outsources cell manufacture; it is only 'investigating cell manufacturing plants in the US and India' (no site).

Planned Atlantis SEZ (Cape Town) Li-ion cell plant: 1.5 GWh initial, 5 GWh peak (S12). Still a proposal: Dec 2024 'unveiled plans ... Atlantis SEZ' with talks with technical partners (S14). Freshness: latest items found are Dec 2024 and a Apr 2026 China Daily interview in which the MD speaks of partnering with Chinese firms but gives no site/financing status; Engineering News (primary) returned 403. No construction, FID or financing evidence; silence suggests stalled but no cancellation evidence so state kept active. ref_year: fallback, searched (no dated phase); S12 page date taken from URL path (2024/02; page shows 'updated 2 June 2026'). start_year/ramp/chemistry/format nulled (v1 unconfirmed). end_market mixed: stationary first, EV medium term (S13). Capacity 5 GWh is 'peak'; some outlets quote 5-10 GWh (unverified).

Aug 2024 reports (S17, S18): protocol of intent with Bahia/Sao Sebastiao do Passe; phase 1 1 GWh (US$109m), 5 GWh in 2028 (S17). A Tarde (S18) also lists 2 GWh yr 2, 5 GWh from yr 4 and 35 GWh 'within 10 years' (undated, aspiration; excluded under D-015, nameplate kept at 5) and construction 'expected Q1 2025' which no source shows happened. STATE DOUBT: a May 2026 S&P Global interview (paywalled/prohibited source, NOT cited; seen only via search summary) reports the project restructured into a ~US$20m pilot, financing stuck on BNDES guarantees, and possibly Camacari rather than Sao Sebastiao do Passe. I could not find an open source, so project_state stays active at low confidence; lead should treat as likely paused/scaled down. chemistry/format/end_market nulled (unconfirmed).

C$1bn Maple Ridge BC redevelopment announced Nov 2023 (S20: up to 135 million cells/yr, construction from June 2024, fully operational 2028). Parent Taiwan Cement confirmed halt of construction Dec 2024 (S19); search found no restart or formal cancellation through 2026 and no timeline to re-evaluate, so paused rather than cancelled. Existing Maple Ridge R&D/cell operations are separate and not this row. v1 nameplate 2.8 GWh nulled: no fetched source gives a GWh/yr figure (only 135M cells; the GWh conversion is not stated). Status under_construction per D-020: S19 confirms 'the stoppage of construction', i.e. works had begun and then stopped (state paused). Chemistry/format/end_market nulled (unconfirmed in fetched pages).

42,000 sq ft pilot manufacturing facility at 7391 Pacific Circle, Mississauga opened (ceremony 2024-10-23 per company blog; the fetched summary did not give a quotable year so start_year left null). Page says it manufactures 'pilot demonstration systems' and assembly lines; no GWh figure, no clear statement that cells are fabricated on site; scope is borderline (zinc-air LDES). Kept as pilot with low confidence rather than removed because no positive evidence it is not a cell/electrochemical-device maker. Nothing newer than 2025 found. Chemistry zinc (zinc-air) and ESS (long-duration storage) from company/press descriptions, not quote-verified.

Pilot zinc-bromide (Endure) line at partner Battery Energy Power Solutions' lead-acid factory, Fairfield NSW; 2 MWh/yr (=0.002 GWh) and 'production line has commenced operations' on 2022-09-30 (S26). installed basis: company/press (same as nameplate; the single line commissioned). Installed figure >18 months old so confidence capped. No news after 2022 found on Endure production; Gelion's FY2025/FY2026 results coverage focuses on sulfur (Li-S) technology and did not mention Endure/Fairfield, so current operation is unconfirmed (may be discontinued). start_year 2022 uses page date (quote carries no separate year). announced_year, cell_format nulled.

Phase 3 pilot pouch-cell line, Geelong VIC: officially opened Aug 2024 (S27, page dated 2024-08-13); still described as 'existing 2 MWh automated production line' on 2025-11-18 (S28). installed basis: company (2 MWh = 0.002 GWh/yr). ref_year: fallback, searched (2025 = publication year of the 2 MWh statement). Separate future plan not included in nameplate: ARENA-backed feasibility (FEL-1) for a stage-based plant 'up to 1 GWh per year' (S28), undated, feasibility stage only -> excluded per D-015; 200 MWh 'Phase 4' older plan superseded. Chemistry is lithium-sulfur (vocab 'other'). start_year nulled: opening quote has no year string (opening Aug 2024). end_market nulled (defence/aerospace/drones, no vocab fit).

Giga-Africa 1: Feb 2025 JV announcement with Dr Henry Mao, start at 1 GWh with 'plans to scale up to 32 GWh' (S15, MarkLines teaser). The 32 GWh is undated with no phase structure -> aspiration under D-015/D-017 (alternatives: keep 32 at <=0.5 with ESCALATE; rejected per lead). Nameplate therefore 1 GWh, ref_year fallback 2025 (publication year of S15). Original 2019 plan (S16) was 32 GWh by 2028 at Coega SEZ with a 2020 pilot that never materialised. CELL-SCOPE DOUBT: phase 1 reportedly uses dry cells made in China with only electrolyte filling and post-processing in South Africa, so the 1 GWh may be finishing capacity rather than full cell manufacture (not in a fetched quote; reported by Engineering News/CI Live summaries). No financing/construction evidence; a March 2026 feasibility study (Engineering News, 403) reportedly ranks Atlantis first and Coega second for a 5-10 GWh plant, suggesting site/scale unsettled. Engineering News and CI Live primary pages unreachable (403/redirect to S&P). Status announced, state active (no cancellation evidence). chemistry (v1 LFP) nulled: not confirmed in fetched pages. jv_partners per S15 (v1 also named Megamillion itself).

CANCELLED. Quebec ended all financing on 2025-09-02/12 after no binding buyer offers; Northvolt Batteries North America insolvent (S4). Nov 2026: Hydro-Quebec reached agreement (pending court approval) to buy the ~1.7 km2 site for a substation/logistics centre; 'construction never went beyond the preparatory stage' (S5, S6). Status kept under_construction per D-020: physical preparatory site works did take place (S5 'stade préparatoire'), the project then stopped and was cancelled. Nameplate = base 30 GWh phase 1 (S4); the 60 GWh is an undated expansion ('expand the site to 60 GWh per year') -> notes only per D-015; ref_year fallback 2025 (publication year of S4). chemistry/format/end_market/announced_year nulled (not confirmed in fetched pages). quebec.ca official statement fetched empty; CBC 403.

On 2026-09-24/25 PowerCo pushed start of operations from 2027 to 2029 and hired EllisDon as general contractor; construction continues (core infrastructure/structural phase) (S1, S3). Treated as a delay, not a pause: state active (candidate routing said paused; rejected because on-site work continues and PowerCo says 'not stepping back'). Nameplate 'up to 90 GWh' (S2, 2025; S1 says 'was once set' and PowerCo is 'determining how and when the facility scales') kept; confidence reduced for that. ref_year: fallback, searched (no dated phase; 2025 = publication year of S2, the source stating the 90 GWh plan; earlier than the 2029 start). Unified cell: prismatic, multi-chemistry (S2), EV. announced_year nulled (not re-fetched). v1 chemistry text normalised to 'mixed'.

Announced Jan 2023: up to 30 GWh/yr, 2 GWh 2024 and 6 GWh 2026 targets (S8). Jun 2023: founder says 'a pause on the Geelong plans, rather than a stop' as Recharge refocused on Britishvolt UK (S7). Other 2023 reports (InnovationAus 403, Bay 939 not fetched) cite no planning applications, no Avalon lease, unpaid staff, tax-crime raid. Status announced, state paused (founder-stated). ref_year: fallback, searched (2023 = publication year of S8; the 2024/2026 ramp targets lapsed). Chemistry/format/end_market nulled. Coordinates left (v1 Geelong city centroid).

Pilot zinc-ion cell line at Dartmouth NS: ~100 batteries/month in 2022 (S30); California Energy Commission 2025 report says the grant 'enabled Salient to increase cell capacity, improve production capability' (S31). Federal grant records (Canada open data, search only) show 2025-26 contributions, i.e. company active. No GWh capacity published, so nameplate null. Planned first gigafactory (USA/Canada, location TBD) is a separate unlocated project. Residential/stationary focus -> ESS (S30 title). Confidence moderate-low: status evidence is a pilot line.

Only evidence is the company's own homepage: a '1MW pilot Na Ion manufacturing facility' described as operational, plus plans for 2 x >1GW large-scale plants (not built, no site/date; not included in nameplate). Location not disclosed anywhere found; page does not say cells vs packs (company says it manufactures Na-ion batteries). 1 MW is power, not GWh/yr. Independent corroboration not found (searches returned only Voltavate, Faradion, QUT sodium-sulfur etc., unrelated). Kept as low-confidence existence-only record; status unconfirmed by any third party.

US$3.2bn, 60 ha RAKEZ site (Al Hamra per S10; Al Ghail per S9), up to 40 GWh at full operation (S9, S10 agree). First line 'fully operational by end of 2026' (S9) -> start_year 2026 as planned value only. Only 2024 coverage exists: land deal done, building permits pending (S9); no groundbreaking, permit approval or schedule update found in any 2025-2026 search; AMS (S11, 2024-10, modified 2025-07) says Statevolt put its US (Imperial Valley) project on hold and is focusing on the UAE and on energy storage (ESS) - so end_market mixed. The 6 GWh first-phase ramp and 'semi-solid-state' were not confirmed in fetched pages: ramp JSON and chemistry nulled (S10: solid-state switch at full capacity). ref_year: fallback, searched (2024 = publication year; no date for full 40 GWh). Silence since 2024 suggests stalled; no evidence for paused/cancelled so stored active. ESCALATE recommendation: paused (no news since 2024 against 'fully operational by end of 2026'), but no open source states a pause.

UniLiB pilot/development plant (Y-TEC + Universidad Nacional de La Plata): Oct 2023 Infobae says prototype Li cells are produced, annual capacity 'unos 15 MWh' (S34) = 0.015 GWh; Nov 2022 article says 13 MWh/yr (S35): sources differ by ~15% -> confidence capped at 0.5. ref_year fallback 2023 (publication year of S34). No 2025-2026 news found on actual output (a 'iProfesional 2026' hit was really dated 2023-07-21); 2023 start dates repeatedly slipped, so operational status rests on the Oct 2023 report. Installed older than 18 months and not separately stated -> null. start_year nulled (quote lacks a year string; inauguration late 2023). chemistry LFP per S34 (electrode raw material). The larger planned Y-TEC industrial plant is a separate project.

Second Rosatom gigafactory, Moscow. Launch reported 2026-10-06/07 (Rosatom announcement; AK&M Russian page dated 2026-10-07; the English AK&M page shows 2026-11-20, apparently the render date) with 4 GWh/yr (S38); Interfax Feb 2026 gave 4 GWh/yr each for Kaliningrad and Moscow and commissioning planned for autumn 2026 (S39); www1.ru Jul 2026: combined 8 GWh/yr for the two plants (S40). Construction began Sept 2023 in Krasnaya Pakhra, New Moscow (PRIME 2025-12-15 per fetch summary, S36 page; location not in a quoted source and coordinates left null). Operator is Rosatom/TVEL subsidiary Renera per search summaries only (not confirmed on a fetched page) so operator stored as Rosatom. Sources are all Russian state-aligned media / Rosatom statements; no independent output data - capacity is design capacity, installed null; the candidate note about 40k test cells was not verified. Interfax also says Sobyanin cites 'two gigafactories' under construction in Krasnaya Pakhra with up to 33 million cells/yr combined; second plant's owner not identified (possible discovery). ref_year: fallback, searched (2026 = commissioning/publication year; no 'full capacity' date).
